reasoning: Set A is the stronger plan. It is more sound on RL and closer to the brief. It defines exact rewards, views and terminal/truncation semantics for all three environments. Its circular tank is one where fish survive as long as possible, which matches the ground truth. It lays out a clear value-learning ladder (tabular → DQN → CNN), with ablations and a 1-D corridor that proves the shared core. It has a REINFORCE→PPO ladder, and self-play with opponent pools and cross-play, which hits the co-evolution/self-play concept head on. Its dependency graph is clean: every spine starts on the interface, and only thicken tasks of the same module serialize. Set A's weaknesses are process narration left in the architecture ('adopted before M1 is built', 'expected values of TC-01–TC-49 don't change'), a brief that still says 'Designing future environments now' is out of scope, pipeline step tables padded with S2/S3 constructors, and a train spine packet that leaves out core.Transition and runs.create_run. Set B has a tidy CLI and pipeline structure and a good method-check gate. But it never specifies a reward function for any world, which is a serious gap for an RL lab whose concepts include reward shaping, and it leaves split builders without an oracle. Its fish tank is a square with respawn and 'hits per fish' scoring, which departs from the circular survive-as-long-as-possible tank. Its predator-prey stage has no self-play or opponent pool, only naive co-training. Its M2 ('See, check and explain') bundles the replay viewer, video, reference check and write-ups into a leftover milestone, so M1 can't show a replay. Its spines also write other owners' modules: the train_loop spine builds runlog.RunWriter, and the DQN spine builds the methods factory.

strengths: Precise, testable spec for all three environments: rewards, views, physics constants, worked examples
Clear concept ladders per stage (tabular/DQN/CNN; REINFORCE/PPO/school/limited view; fixed/naive/pool self-play)
Library comparison carefully scoped (Snake DQN, single-fish PPO, predator vs scripted prey) with a one-to-one settings mapping
Clean dependency graph: all spines depend only on the interface task; serialization only where the same module is thickened
Golden cases in packets are concrete closed-form oracles (e.g. TC-01–TC-10 board states)
weaknesses: Architecture keeps process narration (AD-09/AD-13 'adopted before M1 is built', risk 'TC-01–TC-49 don't change')
Brief is stale: 'Not doing: Designing future environments now' and Snake-only success, while all three are designed
PL-01 step table lists S2/S3 constructors (FishTank, PredatorPrey, PPOAgent, ScriptedPredator), so it doesn't read as a call path; RandomSwimmer appears in two pipelines with different signatures
M1 is a whole stage in one milestone (31 tasks) rather than a skeleton then thickening
Train spine packet omits core.Transition, runs.create_run and runs.GameRecording

strengths: Method check worlds with hand-derived optima gate every batch (a good guard against silent RL bugs)
Well-specified statistical protocol (paired permutation, Holm) and run-folder/seed design
Readable pipelines whose step tables mirror the entry sketches
Replay design (re-simulate into Trace, side by side, sight overlay, video) is thoughtful

weaknesses: No reward function is defined for Snake, the fish tank or predator-prey anywhere in the spec, contract or tests
Fish tank is a square, scored by hits per fish with respawn, which contradicts the circular survive-as-long-as-possible tank
Predator-prey has only naive co-training, with no self-play or opponent pool, so it underserves the co-evolution/self-play concept
M2 'See, check and explain' is a leftover bundle (viewer, video, refcheck, notes, DQN thicken); M1 can't replay
Spines write other owners' modules (T09 builds runlog/writer.py; T08 builds methods/factory.py)
Pipelines' Open questions still list routed items that routes.md marks done
